title: QRÖMELIFE
excerpt: Quavo has released *QRÖMELIFE*, his third solo album, a 14-track record made in close collaboration with Pharrell Williams.
body:
Quavo has released *QRÖMELIFE*, his third solo album, a 14-track record made in close collaboration with Pharrell Williams. The pair spent more than a year and a half building it together, with sessions at Louis Vuitton's headquarters in Paris and on a yacht in Miami.

Quavo has described the goal less as a reinvention than a way to gather the different sides of his music in one place. The melodic phrasing that became central to Migos sits alongside harder Atlanta rhythms and the brighter, more spacious ideas that emerged from his work with Pharrell.

The title comes from what Quavo calls a "qrome" state, the point where pressure, grief and setbacks become part of what a person carries rather than something that simply disappears. That makes *QRÖMELIFE* a different record from *Rocket Power*, the solo album he made while grief over Takeoff was much closer to the surface. The new album does not erase that history, but its focus shifts toward what Quavo has built around it.

[apple:album:6817200688]

One of the clearest signs of that shift is "Away," which brings Offset back onto a Quavo record after the two repaired their relationship. The reunion matters because it arrives without turning the album into a Migos retrospective. Quavo and Offset are working together again and have discussed another Migos project intended to honor Takeoff, but no release date has been announced. On *QRÖMELIFE*, the collaboration is one part of a solo record rather than the entire reason for it.

Fatherhood has also changed the context around the album. Quavo has spoken about having a son and a daughter and about the responsibility of giving them the presence he did not have from his own father, who died when he was young. That idea of moving forward without pretending the losses never happened fits the language he uses around "qrome" and gives the album's emphasis on perseverance a more personal weight.

The rollout introduced that wider sound before the full record arrived. "HAAVIN" first appeared during Pharrell's Louis Vuitton menswear show in Paris, while "Trance (Walk It Down)" pushed further into dance music. Those records made the project feel less like another extension of Quavo's familiar trap template. At the same time, songs such as "Hit-A-Lik" keep Atlanta and the Migos cadence close enough that the album still sounds connected to the career that preceded it.

The chrome visual language runs through the project as deliberately as the music. Quavo worked with Malcolm Ransome on the custom QRÖMELIFE glasses that appear across the album campaign, turning the title into something worn directly across his face. It is a simple image, but it matches the idea behind the record: the experiences Quavo is describing are not presented as a past life to escape, but as something visible in the person who came through them.

Quavo and Offset may eventually carry that story back into another Migos record, but *QRÖMELIFE* does not wait for that possibility. It gives Quavo a full solo project between the grief-centered *Rocket Power* and whatever comes next, with Pharrell helping him widen the sound while the writing keeps returning to family, endurance and the life he has built after loss.
